identification: Korean style bandaji (blanket chest) with brass mounts: bat/butterfly escutcheon plate, diamond studs, hasp, two hinged top panels over a central lock plate, on a low base. Raw timber interior, dark stained exterior, one top panel detached. Looks 20th century (mid century or later), probably a decorator or reproduction piece, not a 19th century chest. Photos show well-made mounts and a plinth base but no maker marks.

viewing_check: Check the age and build: dovetails or nails, thickness and wear on the timber, patina on the brass (cast and aged vs thin stamped and shiny), and whether the interior raw wood is old or fresh. Check the detached panel is present and whether the hinges or its fixings are broken. Look for fitted lock and key and any maker label or underside marks. Heavy genuine old brass mounts and old timber would lift it above reproduction value.
